A chart is a smooth coordinate map; an observer congruence is a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$; its integral curves, an adapted chart, and a tetrad field are distinct objects. The exact regularity and rest-space conventions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and the chart/congruence distinction of [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] apply. An orthogonal family of rest slices is not available for every congruence.

For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

The constant $c$ supplies the spacetime length/time conversion. In a branch with dynamical Einstein gravity, $G$ is an independent coupling parameter in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The Boltzmann constant $k_B$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is used when a statistical entropy/temperature calibration is adopted. Planck's constant $h_{\rm P}=2\pi\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$; $\hbar$ is used only in a quantum branch. Under the current SI definition, $c$, $h_{\rm P}$ and $k_B$ have exact defining numerical values; this metrological fact does not make them derived predictions of a thermodynamic or gravitational model. $G$ is experimentally adjusted and carries measurement uncertainty. The local energy function, pressure, temperature and chemical potential in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] are derived from the supplied state function; no particle mass or universal equation of state is derived from gravity alone.

For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on an open domain, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ by [[def-gr-killing-field]], restrict attention to a domain where $\xi$ is future timelike and choose a positive normalization at infinity or at a specified wall/observer. $$g=-e^{2\phi(r)}(dx^0)^2+b(r)^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma.$$
Set $N=\partial_{x^0}$ as time orientation. The signature convention is $(-,+,+,+)$, $x^0$ and $r$ are measured in metres, the line element has units $\mathrm m^2$, and $\phi$ and $b$ are dimensionless. The sphere at fixed $(x^0,r)$ has induced metric $r^2\gamma$ and area $4\pi r^2$, so $r$ is the areal radius. The metric is static in the precise sense that its coefficients are independent of $x^0$, and $N$ is a timelike Killing vector field because $g(N,N)=-e^{2\phi}<0$.

A **static isotropic diagonal source field** is a mixed tensor field in the sense of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]], with its smooth tensor type fixed by [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and is defined globally using the product splitting $TM\cong TI_0\oplus T(0,\infty)\oplus TS^2$: it acts by $-\epsilon(r)$ on the time factor, by $p(r)$ on the radial factor, and by $p(r)$ times the identity on $TS^2$. In every standard spherical chart its mixed components are
$$T^a{}_b=\operatorname{diag}(-\epsilon(r),p(r),p(r),p(r)),$$
where $\epsilon,p\in C^\infty((0,\infty),\mathbb R)$; its lowered form is symmetric because both $g$ and this diagonal field are diagonal. For formula bookkeeping in SI dimensions, assign $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, $[G]=\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, and $[c]=\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Define the mass function
$$M(r):=\frac{c^2r}{2G}\bigl(1-b(r)\bigr),$$
which has units $\mathrm{kg}$. No Einstein equation, equation of state, central regularity, physical applicability, or empirical claim is part of this definition. The Einstein tensor and component conventions used later are those of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] and [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]].

Assume the countable-choice convention ZF+$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ used by the exact geometry supplier [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Use its product spacetime, areal radius $r$, time coordinate $x^0=ct$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and static metric
$$g=-e^{2\phi(r)}(dx^0)^2+b(r)^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma,$$
where $\gamma$ is the unit round metric, $b(r)>0$, and the metric coefficients are independent of $x^0$. Here $x^0$ and $r$ are in metres, $\phi$ and $b$ are dimensionless, $G>0$ is in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and $c>0$ is in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, as in [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. The static unit fluid velocity is $u=e^{-\phi}\partial_{x^0}$.

For an open pressure interval $I_P\subset(0,\infty)$, supply a $C^\infty$ constitutive function $\mathcal E:I_P\to(0,\infty)$, with pressure and energy-density values both in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. On any open radial interval $J\subset(0,\infty)$ occupied by the fluid, let $P\in C^\infty(J,I_P)$; that is, $P$ is a smooth real-valued function and $P(r)\in I_P$ for every $r\in J$. Identify $P$ with the pressure component $p|_J$ of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]] and set $\varepsilon|_J=\mathcal E\circ P\in C^\infty(J,(0,\infty))$. Adopt the $\Lambda=0$ Einstein field equation on $J$
$$G^a{}_b=\frac{8\pi G}{c^4}T^a{}_b,\qquad T^a{}_b|_J=\operatorname{diag}(-\mathcal E(P(r)),P(r),P(r),P(r)),$$
with the signed curvature and Einstein-tensor conventions of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Thus “perfect fluid” here means exactly this static isotropic rest-frame stress tensor on the stated fluid interval; the EOS is a supplied model input, not derived from gravity. This formulation asserts no smoothness across an interface with vacuum or another matter region; any piecewise matching is a separate condition.

This is an adopted classical model and source of conditional predictions. The cited treatments motivate the static-fluid and EOS conventions; the later local branch and constant-density results are established only by their displayed conditional arguments and mathematical suppliers.

Assume $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, where $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is exactly [[def-countable-choice]] and is inherited from the smooth Lorentzian/tensor suppliers. Let $\epsilon:I_p\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^\infty$ on an open interval $I_p\subseteq(0,\infty)$, let $P_c\subset I_p$ be a nonempty compact interval, and choose $\delta>0$ such that the closed $\delta$-neighbourhood of $P_c$ lies in $I_p$. Fix $\phi_c\in\mathbb R$ and use the units and signature of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Put $K=4\pi G/c^4$, with formal units $\mathrm m\,\mathrm J^{-1}$; $v$ has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$. There is $R_0>0$, common to all $p_c\in P_c$, such that for each $p_c$ there is a unique pair of even continuous functions $p,v$ on $[-R_0,R_0]$ with $|p(r)-p_c|\le\delta$ and satisfying
$$v(r)=K\int_0^1 s^2\epsilon(p(rs))\,ds,\qquad p(r)=p_c-\int_0^r t\frac{(\epsilon(p(t))+p(t))(v(t)+Kp(t))}{1-2t^2v(t)}\,dt.$$
They are $C^\infty$, $p(0)=p_c$, $v(0)=K\epsilon(p_c)/3$, $p'(0)=v'(0)=0$, and $b(r):=1-2r^2v(r)\ge1/2$ on $[0,R_0]$. Define
$$M(r)=\frac{c^2}{G}r^3v(r),\qquad \phi(r)=\phi_c+\int_0^r t\frac{v(t)+Kp(t)}{1-2t^2v(t)}\,dt\quad(|r|\le R_0).$$
Then $(M,p,\phi)$ satisfies the mass, pressure, and lapse equations of [[lem-tgr-spherical-einstein-tov-reduction]] for $0<r\le R_0$. The metric extends across $r=0$ as a $C^2$ Lorentzian metric in Cartesian spatial coordinates, with $b(0)=1$ and lapse $e^{\phi_c}>0$; this is the regular-center conclusion in this item. On the common interval, $p,v,\phi$ depend continuously in the uniform norm on $p_c\in P_c$. For $r>0$, the solution continues past any finite endpoint at which its graph remains in a compact subset of
$$\{(r,p,v):r>0,\ p\in I_p,\ 1-2r^2v>0\}.$$
No assertion is made that every equation of state reaches a zero-pressure surface, avoids a horizon globally, or gives a dynamically stable solution.

Assume $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ exactly as in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $J\subseteq(0,\infty)$ be an open interval; let the state domain, metric, mixed source tensor, mass function, units, and signature be those of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Write $\kappa=8\pi G/c^4$, and let $G^a{}_b$ be the mixed Einstein tensor defined from the signed curvature convention in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Suppose $\phi,b,\epsilon,p$ are smooth on $J$ and $b>0$. As a conditional mathematical system, assume the component equations
$$G^a{}_b=\kappa T^a{}_b.$$
Then on $J$,
$$M'=\frac{4\pi r^2\epsilon}{c^2},\qquad \phi'=\frac{GM/c^2+4\pi G r^3p/c^4}{r^2b},\qquad p'=-\frac{G(\epsilon+p)(M+4\pi r^3p/c^2)}{c^2r^2b}.$$
Conversely, if these three ordinary differential equations hold with $M=c^2r(1-b)/(2G)$, then every mixed Einstein component satisfies $G^a{}_b=\kappa T^a{}_b$. The identity $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$ used for this converse is the geometric theorem of [[thm-gr-second-bianchi-and-divergence-free-einstein]], not a field equation or empirical premise. This lemma is a pure conditional calculation and makes no claim that the model describes nature.

The constructed profiles satisfy the mass, pressure, and lapse equations in [F3] on $r>0$, with $\varepsilon(r)=\mathcal E(P(r))$ and $b>0$. The converse direction of [F3] therefore gives every mixed Einstein component of the adopted model on the punctured neighborhood. A $C^2$ metric has a continuous Einstein tensor; equality on the punctured neighborhood therefore extends to the center.

Put $a=\sqrt{1-u}$ and $B(r)=\sqrt{1-ur^2/R^2}$. For $0\le r\le R$, the adopted model has the explicit profiles
$$M(r)=M_R(r/R)^3,\quad b(r)=B(r)^2,\quad P(r)=\varepsilon_0\frac{B(r)-a}{3a-B(r)},\quad e^{\phi(r)}=\frac{3a-B(r)}2.$$
For $r\ge R$, set $M(r)=M_R$, $b(r)=1-2GM_R/(c^2r)$, $P(r)=0$, $\varepsilon(r)=0$, and $e^{\phi(r)}=\sqrt{b(r)}$. Then the interior is a regular static Einstein-fluid solution through the center, the exterior is vacuum, and the join at $r=R$ is $C^1$ and piecewise $C^2$ with no delta-supported surface stress. The central pressure is finite and equals $P(0)=\varepsilon_0(1-a)/(3a-1)$. This conclusion is specific to the constant-density branch $0<u<8/9$.

Then $2GM_n/(c^2R_n)=8\pi G\varepsilon_0R_n^2/(3c^4)=u_n\in(0,8/9)$, so every $(\rho_0,R_n)$ is an admissible member of [F1] at the fixed density. Moreover $a_n=\sqrt{1-u_n}=\sqrt{1/9+1/n}>1/3$ and $a_n\downarrow1/3$.

By [F1], $P_n(0)/\varepsilon_0=(1-a_n)/(3a_n-1)$. The numerator tends to $2/3>0$ and the denominator tends to $0$ through positive values, so the ratios tend to $+\infty$. Therefore no finite $K_0$ can bound all ratios, refuting the displayed statement. At the limiting value $u=8/9$, the denominator is zero and the endpoint is not an admissible regular finite-pressure member.

Assume the finite-bath preparation [[post-tgr-finite-bath-exchange-preparation]], which supplies $C^2$ subsystem and bath entropies on open energy intervals, with subsystem temperature $T_*>0$, finite capacity $C_G<0$, bath capacity $C_b$ satisfying $0<C_b<|C_G|$, conserved total energy, and exchange law $\dot x=L S_{\rm tot}'(x)$ for $L>0$. At the matched-temperature point $x_*$,
$$S_{\rm tot}''(x_*)=-\frac1{T_*^2}\left(\frac1{C_G}+\frac1{C_b}\right)<0.$$
Consequently $x_*$ is a strict local entropy maximum in this energy-exchange direction, the adopted ODE has a forward-invariant local basin with exponential attraction to $x_*$, and along each solution $dS_{\rm tot}/dt=L(S_{\rm tot}')^2\ge0$. These are properties of the selected scalar exchange model only.

derivations.claim: With $C_b=|C_G|/2$, the bath capacity is positive and satisfies $C_b<|C_G|$. Setting $E_b=E_0+C_bT_*$ gives $T_b=(E_b-E_0)/C_b=T_*$, so the selected state is common-temperature as required in [F1].

Since $C_G<0$, $1/C_G=-1/|C_G|$ and $1/C_b=2/|C_G|$. Hence [F1] gives $S_{\rm tot}''(x_*)=-1/(T_*^2|C_G|)<0$ and its stated local exponential attraction and nonnegative entropy production. This is the specified exchange ODE, not a stellar evolution law.
